audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL-focused specifications: bloom filter construction (Prague), KECCAK256 opcode execution, EVM tracing infrastructure, EIP-155 replay protection, RIPEMD-160 precompile, EIP-8077 transaction announcements (P2P), EIP-1459 DNS node discovery, EIP-2256 wallet asset queries, EIP-2028 calldata gas repricing, and EIP-7692 EOF validation. All are EL-centric with no material CL content.

el_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions, resource exhaustion via bloom filter queries, replay attacks across chains, privacy leakage via asset queries
Eclipse attacks, false transaction announcement metadata, protocol violation, bandwidth exhaustion via oversized announcements
Deploy malformed EOF bytecode attempting to bypass validation, resource exhaustion via complex initcode
Eclipse attacks by controlling discovered node list, DNS poisoning, sequence rollback attacks

cl_vectors.threat: Propose invalid blocks, submit conflicting attestations, censorship
Provide incorrect data, censorship, denial of service

misclassified_entities.reason: Transaction Execution Engine is an internal EL component (EVM), not an external entity. It produces log entries within the system boundary.
Calling Contract is an internal EVM entity executing within the same system boundary. Precompile calls are internal EVM dispatches, not cross-boundary interactions.
The Ethereum Client performing DNS discovery is the system itself, not an external entity. The external entities are the DNS resolver and the DNS list publisher.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC (Log Queries)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated RPC client submitting log filter queries. Query parameters (address, topics) are untrusted and could be crafted for resource exhaustion via bloom filter lookups.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC (Transaction Submission)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated RPC endpoint. Transactions may be malformed, have invalid signatures, wrong chain IDs, or insufficient gas. Full validation required including EIP-155 chain ID verification, intrinsic gas calculation (EIP-2028), and EOF validation (EIP-7692).

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet/Signer via Transaction Broadcast
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External wallet produces signed transactions. The EL must validate the signature, chain ID, and v parameter format. A compromised wallet could produce replay-vulnerable legacy transactions (v=27/28).

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P (Transaction Announcements)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P peer. EIP-8077 adds sender address and nonce to announcements, but this metadata is NOT cryptographically verified. Must be treated as optimization hints only, never for security decisions. Peers can send arbitrary false metadata.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P (Transaction Data)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Full transaction data from peers must be validated: signature verification, metadata match against announcement, chain ID, gas limits. Protocol violations (metadata mismatch) should penalize the peer.

trusted_external_entities.name: DNS Resolver via DNS Protocol
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: DNS TXT record responses (EIP-1459 enrtree protocol)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DNS infrastructure is untrusted. Responses could be poisoned, corrupted, or replayed. Integrity is verified via Merkle tree hash verification and root record signature verification against a known secp256k1 public key. Sequence number checks prevent rollback attacks.

trusted_external_entities.name: DNS List Publisher via Signed Root Record
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Publisher signs the root record with a secp256k1 key embedded in the enrtree URL. Signature is verified, so data integrity is authenticated. However, a trusted publisher can still perform eclipse attacks by only including nodes they control. Multiple independent sources should be used.

trusted_external_entities.name: Client Configuration (enrtree URLs)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Configuration is set by the node operator. Trusted in terms of authenticity but the enrtree URLs determine which DNS publishers are trusted, which is a critical trust decision affecting eclipse resistance.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via Wallet RPC (Asset Queries)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Untrusted web3 application requesting user asset information. The dApp identity may be spoofed. The justification parameter cannot be trusted. User consent is required before sharing any data. Request parameters (address, chainId, types) must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Deployer via Creation Transaction
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Contract creation transaction (EOFCREATE / initcode tx per EIP-7692)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Untrusted entity deploying bytecode. EOF containers must pass full structural validation (header, type section, code sections, data section), code validation (valid opcodes per EIP-3670), and static stack analysis (EIP-5450). Both initcode and deployed code must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer via P2P (Block Propagation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block producers could craft blocks with maximal calldata to exploit reduced gas costs (EIP-2028: 16 gas per non-zero byte vs previous 68). Large blocks increase propagation delay, threatening network security per Sompolinsky-Zohar model.

trusted_external_entities.name: Replay Attacker via Cross-Chain Broadcast
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attacker captures transactions on chain A and replays them on chain B. EIP-155 chain ID in the v parameter provides protection for new transactions, but legacy transactions (v=27/28) remain vulnerable. Full chain ID validation is required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Debugging Tool via Tracer API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Debugging tools configure custom tracers that receive sensitive EVM state (stack, memory, storage). Authenticated via local API access. However, tracer implementations could leak sensitive data or cause performance degradation. The tracer receives direct references to EVM internal state.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Filter parameters (address, topics) must be validated. Bloom filter checks provide O(1) elimination but false positives require full log scan. Rate limiting may be needed to prevent resource exhaustion from excessive queries.

Full transaction validation required: RLP decoding, signature verification, EIP-155 chain ID check, intrinsic gas calculation (EIP-2028 rates), nonce verification, balance check. For EOF transactions, initcode and deployed code must pass EOF validation.

v parameter must be checked: v=27/28 for legacy (no replay protection), v=CHAIN_ID*2+35/36 for EIP-155. Chain ID extracted from v must match network. Invalid v values must be rejected. Nine-element RLP hash used for EIP-155 recovery.

Announced sender address and nonce are UNVERIFIED and must never be used for security decisions. Use only as optimization hints for request prioritization. Validate metadata against actual transaction after retrieval. Flag protocol violations on mismatch.

Full transaction validation required. Compare hash, type, size, address, nonce against announcement metadata. Mismatch constitutes protocol violation; peer should be penalized/disconnected after threshold.

All DNS responses must be verified: root record signature against known public key, branch/leaf content against subdomain keccak256 hash, sequence number against cached value (reject rollbacks). Records exceeding 512 bytes must be rejected.

Signature verification ensures data integrity but not node quality. Publisher could perform eclipse attacks by curating node list. Multiple independent DNS sources must be used. Sequence number must be monotonically increasing.

Configuration determines which publishers are trusted. Node operator must verify enrtree URL authenticity. Using a single source increases eclipse attack risk. Multiple independent sources recommended.

Request parameters must be validated (address format, chainId, limit, types). User consent is mandatory before returning asset data. Only whitelisted assets should be shared. DApp identity cannot be trusted (phishing risk). Justification parameter is informational only.

EOF container must pass: magic byte check (0xEF00), structural validation (header, sections), code validation (valid opcodes per EIP-3670), static stack analysis (no underflow/overflow per EIP-5450), return stack depth limits. Both initcode and deployed code validated independently.

Blocks with large calldata payloads (enabled by EIP-2028 reduced pricing) must still propagate within acceptable delay bounds. Intrinsic gas validation ensures minimum gas coverage. Block gas limit provides upper bound on total calldata size.

EIP-155 transactions must have chain ID matching the local network. Legacy transactions (v=27/28) lack replay protection and may be valid on multiple chains. Nodes should enforce EIP-155 format for post-Spurious Dragon transactions.

Tracer API should be restricted to authorized local access only. Custom tracers receive sensitive EVM state (stack, memory, PC, gas). Tracers must not modify EVM state. Performance impact of tracers should be bounded. Default tracer (discard) must be active unless explicitly configured.
